title: Sports Minister Natalia Duco Resigns Amid Government-Vehicle Scandal
detail: President Kast accepted the resignation of Sports Minister Natalia Duco and Undersecretary Andrés Otero, announced the night of August 13 and effective August 14, after a Contraloría complaint over misuse of an official government vehicle. Duco had claimed the car was used for a work meeting, but a video showed it being used for a recreational gathering with karaoke, drinks, and an asado. The vehicle episode capped months of controversy at the Sports Ministry, including a Proddar scholarship payment irregularity flagged by the Contraloría and the abrupt, later-reversed cancellation of a BTS concert at Estadio Nacional. Kast named Francisco Riveros as the new Sports Minister the same day.

media.caption: Natalia Duco resigns as Sports Minister amid fiscal-vehicle scandal — August 13, 2026

title: 'Operación Cancerbero': Gendarmería Transfers Nearly 300 High-Risk Inmates to New Talca Maximum-Security Prison
detail: Gendarmería, with Carabineros and PDI support and two-helicopter escort, carried out 'Operación Cancerbero' on August 13, transferring high-risk inmates — including organized-crime leaders and members — from prisons across the country (Arica, Alto Hospicio, Puente Alto, Colina 1, Colina 2, Puerto Montt, and others) to the new La Laguna maximum-security prison in Talca, modeled explicitly on El Salvador's Bukele-style penal system. President Kast traveled to the Maule region with Justice Minister Fernando Rabat and Security Minister Martín Arrau to oversee the operation. The new regime imposes individual segregation, constant facial-recognition monitoring, and only two hours of yard time for the most dangerous inmates.

media.caption: 'Operación Cancerbero' transfers high-risk inmates to new Talca maximum-security prison — August 13, 2026

title: White House Report Names Chile Among Countries Used by China to Evade US Tariffs
detail: A 25-page White House report titled 'The Great Transshipment Scam,' released August 13, listed Chile among more than 40 countries flagged for transshipment risk, grouping it with Argentina, Colombia, Panama, and Peru as a 'small opportunistic Chinese target' offering cheap labor, free trade zones, port access, and limited customs oversight, and separately naming it as part of a Pacific/Atlantic route-diversion corridor for Chinese goods. The report followed the US Trade Representative's early-August decision to apply an additional 12.5% tariff on Chilean imports over an alleged failure to block goods made with forced labor — a finding the Kast government has disputed, arguing Chile has robust labor institutions, while Chilean exporters and right-wing politicians said the real driver was US pressure over Chile's trade ties with China.

media.caption: White House report names Chile among countries used by China to evade US tariffs — August 13, 2026
